At 2005-08-19 13:56:00 two I/O nodes on R43-M0, R43-M0-NC-I:J18-U01 and R43-M0-N8-I:J18-U11, each logged a FATAL KERNEL "kernel panic" a fraction of a second apart. The context window shows no log lines on any node in the 30 min before them, and no further lines after the second panic within the 30 min after.
Scope: bgl dataset, 2005-08-19 (day-wide R43 search 00:00 → 24:00; context window 13:26:00 → 14:26:00; pattern history over the whole corpus). Filter location=R43, because location=R43-M0 and R43/M0 returned 0 matches in these searches. Results were not truncated except the pattern 576 history (10 of 18 rows shown).
First panic: line 3069219, 2005-08-19 13:56:00.280831, KERNEL FATAL, node R43-M0-NC-I:J18-U01, body "kernel panic" (pattern_id 576).
Second panic: line 3069220, 2005-08-19 13:56:00.628434, KERNEL FATAL, node R43-M0-N8-I:J18-U11, body "kernel panic".
Within R43-M0 only these two nodes logged in the 13:40:00 → 14:10:00 window: 2 log lines across 2 locations, one line each.
Before the first panic: the ±1800 s context window holds 0 log lines on any node (before_total 0). The nearest earlier line in the dataset is 2005-08-19 13:17:11.356019, node R73-M1-N1-C:J16-U11, "total of 1 ddr error(s) detected and corrected", 2328.9 s before the anchor, on a different rack.
The last earlier R43 lines were at 2005-08-19 12:26:12.802459 and 12:26:12.894104 on R43-M0-NC-I:J18-U11 and R43-M0-NC-I:J18-U01: "ciod: LOGIN chdir(/home/auselton/testing) failed: No such file or directory" (pattern 586, FATAL). Earlier ciod lines at 12:26:09 on R43-M0-N8-I:J18-U11/U01 read "ciod: Error reading message prefix after LOGIN_MESSAGE on CioStream socket to 172.16.96.116:40777: Link has been severed" (pattern 435).
After the panics: after_total is 1 inside the window (the second panic). The nearest later line in the dataset is 2005-08-19 17:11:25.056627, node R56-M1-N0-I:J18-U01, "ciod: LOGIN chdir(/home/auselton/testing) failed: No such file or directory", 11724.8 s after the anchor. The next R43 line is 2005-08-19 17:12:18.570717 on R43-M1-NC-I:J18-U11 (same ciod chdir message).
R43 logged 37 log lines on 2005-08-19 across 17 locations, first 2005-08-19 12:24:41.458315 and last 2005-08-19 23:28:05.646975. The only KERNEL FATAL lines in R43 that day are the two panics.
Recurring, not new: pattern 576 ("kernel panic") has 18 matches on 18 distinct nodes, first 2005-08-15 16:31:53.274944 and last 2005-11-11 13:51:11.907657. Other sampled bursts include R57-M1-NC-I:J18-U01 at 2005-08-23 12:11:21.154182 and R04-M0-N8-I:J18-U01 at 2005-08-15 16:31:53.274944. All sampled panic nodes are J18 I/O-card nodes.
Rate vs usual: pattern 576 had 2 log lines in 2005-08-19 13:00:00 → 14:00:00 (window_rate_per_h 2.0) versus a baseline_rate_per_h of 0.004 (baseline_lines 3 over 720 windows), ratio 480.0. This rate covers the whole dataset, not only R43.
Hypothesis: The two I/O nodes may have panicked from the same underlying event, such as a shared job, filesystem or I/O-network problem. The ciod LOGIN chdir and "Link has been severed" errors on the same nodes at 12:26 may be related, though they sit about 1.5 h earlier. Would confirm: Run precursors(576) and compare what precedes each panic burst; check the I/O node console/RAS logs outside this dataset around 13:56 and whether the same job or user was running on R43-M0 at 12:26 and 13:56.
Unknown: Root cause of the kernel panic: the log line is just "kernel panic" with no stack or reason.
Unknown: Whether the nodes rebooted, recovered or stayed down, and any job or customer impact, cost or downtime. None of this is in the logs checked.
Unknown: Why searches with location R43-M0 or R43/M0 returned 0 matches, while location R43 found the lines.
Next step: Run precursors(pattern_id=576) and spread(pattern_id=576), then a get_context with before_s/after_s up to 86400 on line 3069219 for scope R43. — The ±1800 s window showed no preceding lines. A wider window and the other panic bursts (2005-08-15, 2005-08-23) would show whether the ciod errors or anything else regularly precedes the panic.
Next step: Inspect the R43-M0 I/O nodes R43-M0-NC-I:J18-U01 and R43-M0-N8-I:J18-U11: boot/uptime, console output at 13:56:00 and the job allocated to them. — Both nodes panicked within the same second (13:56:00.280831 and 13:56:00.628434), and only these two R43-M0 nodes logged in the 13:40:00 → 14:10:00 window.

new.text:
Two FATAL KERNEL "kernel panic" log lines (pattern 576) hit I/O nodes R43-M0-NC-I:J18-U01 and R43-M0-N8-I:J18-U11 at 2005-08-19 13:56:00. They were the only log lines in the dataset from 13:50:00 to 14:02:00. Pattern 576 is a recurring pattern, not new.
Scope: Dataset bgl, 2005-08-19 13:50 to 14:02 for the panic window, with wider context from 2005-08-18 13:56 to 2005-08-20 13:56 on location R43/R43-M0 and 2005-08-19 11:56 to 15:56 across all locations. The R43/M0 and R43-M0 location filters matched 0 log lines (probably the wrong location format). The R43 and R43/R43-M0 filters worked. The context lists were limited to 10 lines per side and are truncated.
A FATAL KERNEL "kernel panic" (pattern 576) was logged on node R43-M0-NC-I:J18-U01 at 2005-08-19 13:56:00.280831 (line_id 3069219).
A second FATAL KERNEL "kernel panic" was logged on node R43-M0-N8-I:J18-U11 at 2005-08-19 13:56:00.628434 (line_id 3069220). The R43 search for 13:00 to 15:00 returned 2 log lines on 2 nodes.
In the whole dataset, the line immediately before the first panic was an INFO line at 2005-08-19 13:17:11.356019 on R73-M1-N1-C:J16-U11: "total of 1 ddr error(s) detected and corrected". It is on a different rack, not R43.
On R43/R43-M0, the closest earlier lines were at 2005-08-19 12:26:12.894104 on R43-M0-NC-I:J18-U01: FATAL APP "ciod: LOGIN chdir(/home/auselton/testing) failed: No such file or directory". Other R43-M0 nodes logged the same message at 12:24:59 to 12:26:12.
At 2005-08-19 12:26:09.107203, node R43-M0-N8-I:J18-U11 logged FATAL "ciod: Error reading message prefix after LOGIN_MESSAGE on CioStream socket to 172.16.96.116:40777: Link has been severed". This is the same node that panicked at 13:56:00.628434.
After the second panic, the next line anywhere in the dataset was at 2005-08-19 17:11:25.056627 on R56-M1-N0-I:J18-U01: FATAL APP "ciod: LOGIN chdir(/home/auselton/testing) failed: No such file or directory", 11724.8 seconds after the first panic.
On R43/R43-M0, the first lines after the panics were at 2005-08-19 17:12:37.933881 on R43-M0-N8-I:J18-U11 and then on R43-M0-N4, N0 and NC I/O nodes, all "ciod: LOGIN chdir(/home/auselton/testing) failed: No such file or directory". The N8-I:J18-U01 node logged a "Link has been severed" line at 17:12:38.028933.
Pattern 576 ("kernel panic", team node-platform) has 18 log lines, 13 bursts, 18 nodes and 8 weeks active, from 2005-08-15T16:31:53.274944 to 2005-11-11T13:51:11.907657. Before this event it had 2 bursts and 3 log lines, so it is recurring. The median gap between bursts is 5 days, 1:01:37.812071.
By month, pattern 576 started 5 bursts (10 log lines) in 2005-08, 2 bursts in 2005-09, 3 in 2005-10 and 3 in 2005-11.
Hypothesis: The panics on these I/O nodes may be linked to the ciod/CioStream connection problems seen on the same midplane earlier ("Link has been severed" on R43-M0-N8-I:J18-U11, and the repeated LOGIN chdir failures). A ciod or file-system problem could have left the I/O node kernel in a bad state. Would confirm: Check what precedes the other pattern 576 bursts (precursors for pattern_id 576). If the same ciod LOGIN/link-severed lines recur before panics on other I/O nodes, the link holds. If not, it is probably coincidence.
Unknown: The root cause of the kernel panic is not in these logs, since the line body is only "kernel panic".
Unknown: The usual rate of panics on R43-M0 specifically was not measured. Only the dataset-wide pattern history is available.
Unknown: Job, customer or downtime impact is not in the logs.

Just before (same node): at 2005-11-17 05:33:24.491562 R77-M0-NC-I:J18-U11 logged KERNEL/INFO 'ciod: Received signal 15, code=0, errno=0, address=0x000001b0'. The same signal-15 then error-reading-prefix pair repeats on R77-M0-N4-I:J18-U11 (05:33:24.852317 then 05:33:24.982940) and on R77-M1-NC-I:J18-U01 (05:33:25.183395 then 05:33:25.311353).

The 'ciod: Received signal 15' wording has 0 matches before 2005-11-17 00:00:00. Pattern 960 (signal 15) first appears at 2005-11-17 05:14:17.105933 on R65-M0-N4-I:J18-U11, ahead of the first pattern-968 line. It has 39457 log lines across 1024 nodes from that date onward.

Also before the anchor, on R63 compute nodes (…-C:…), 64 log lines of pattern 966 ('1 torus receiver x- input pipe error(s) (dcr 0x02ed) detected and corrected over 43 seconds') ran from 2005-11-17 05:33:06.561436 to 05:33:24.160372 on 64 distinct nodes. Pattern 967 torus sender retransmission lines are interleaved, e.g. '4167003 torus sender x- retransmission error(s) (dcr 0x02f5) detected and corrected over 76 seconds' at 05:33:24.287417. All are severity INFO and on different nodes from the I/O nodes that logged the FATAL lines.

The context window held 603 log lines before the anchor and 192 after it. The nearest earlier line outside the window is a ddr-error line at 2005-11-17 05:03:10.541845 on R60-M0-N2-C:J12-U11, 1814.1 seconds before. The nearest later line is another pattern-968 line at 05:33:54.735514 on R46-M1-NC-I:J18-U11, 30.1 seconds after.

In the 2005-11-17 04:30:00 → 05:34:00 window there are 1092 log lines on 351 distinct nodes. The latest 30 are almost all ciod signal-15 and 'Link has been severed' pairs, with a few signal-15 lines having no error line shown next to them.

Recurring family: an earlier variant, 'ciod: Error reading message prefix after LOGIN_MESSAGE on CioStream socket to 172.16.96.116:56214: Link has been severed' (pattern 435), first appears at 2005-07-20 11:54:27.005995 on R03-M1-N8-I:J18-U01. The wider text search over the corpus gives 49651 matches. The 2005-11-17 wording (pattern 968) is new in this corpus, but the same failure family had occurred before.
Daily pattern-968 log lines vary widely after the start, from 0 on several days to 3466 on 2005-11-26. 2005-11-17 is the first day it appears and is not the peak.

hypotheses.statement: A job or control-system action sent SIGTERM (signal 15) to ciod on many I/O nodes, for example a partition or job kill or reboot. The ciod sockets to 172.16.96.116 then closed, which produced 'Link has been severed'. The corrected torus errors on R63 compute nodes are probably unrelated, since they are INFO, on other nodes and already corrected.
hypotheses.would_confirm: Logs of the host at 172.16.96.116 (the service or control node) around 2005-11-17 05:14–05:34 showing a kill, shutdown or partition action. Also check whether the signal-15 lines are grouped by job or partition.

unknowns: The logs do not establish who or what sent signal 15, or why.
Whether the torus errors on R63 relate to the ciod failures cannot be determined from these lines.
Customer impact, downtime and cost are not in the logs.
The full per-node ordering for all 1024 nodes was not checked; only samples and the 30-second window were read.

Yes. Six VMs had abnormally slow spawn and build times. The worst was a445709b-6ad0-40ec-8860-bec60b6ca0c2, with a build time of 51.59 s against a median of 20.55 s (ratio 2.51). Every other flagged VM was at least 1.14 times the median. The logs don't show which node ran any of them.
Scope: Dataset openstack, 2017-05-14 19:39:22 → 2017-05-17 06:25:06. Filter: dataset only. Baseline is each message pattern over the whole dataset, with threshold = max(median + 6×MAD, median + 2 s). The outlier results were not truncated. The search_logs result was a 5-row sample of 2066 matches. The context window around line 16731 was truncated at 30 lines per side.
The outlier scan flagged 16 log lines on 6 distinct objects. The flagged lines include VM spawn and build step lines (pattern 100016 and pattern 100017, 6 flagged each) plus a few HTTP request lines, which are not VM starts.
The build baseline (pattern 100017, 'Took N seconds to build instance') has n 2066, median 20.55 s, p95 21.81 s and threshold 23.07 s. 6 lines were flagged. The spawn baseline (pattern 100016) has n 2066, median 19.74 s, p95 21.008 s and threshold 22.26 s. 6 lines were flagged.
Worst VM a445709b-6ad0-40ec-8860-bec60b6ca0c2 (nova-compute, 2017-05-14 21:43:33): '[instance: a445709b-6ad0-40ec-8860-bec60b6ca0c2] Took 50.72 seconds to spawn the instance on the hypervisor.' (ratio 2.57 vs median 19.74) and '[instance: a445709b-6ad0-40ec-8860-bec60b6ca0c2] Took 51.59 seconds to build instance.' (ratio 2.51 vs median 20.55).
Other slow VMs, by build time against the 20.55 s median: 544fd51c-4edc-4780-baae-ba1d80a0acfc 42.81 s (ratio 2.08, spawn 41.81 s); 1643649d-2f42-4303-bfcd-7798baec19f9 32.12 s (ratio 1.56, spawn 31.27 s); ae651dff-c7ad-43d6-ac96-bbcd820ccca8 30.32 s (ratio 1.48, spawn 29.46 s); d7d68893-c44f-4e7c-8d4b-0e7801d62776 27.61 s (ratio 1.34, spawn 26.69 s); f0ff0b46-b3cd-43e6-97eb-839fd1cdaa87 23.34 s (ratio 1.14, spawn 22.56 s), only just over the threshold.
Timing: five of the six VMs were flagged between 2017-05-14T21:08:19.736000 and 2017-05-14T21:47:20.593000. The sixth, f0ff0b46-b3cd-43e6-97eb-839fd1cdaa87, was flagged at 2017-05-16T16:49:11.697000. So this is recurring across at least two dates, not a single event.
Timeline before the worst VM's slow build (request req-5b5b0c22-ccce-41fc-8438-ceb520b5a8c2): 21:42:41.757 nova-api 'POST /v2/54fadb412c4e40cdbaed9335e4c35a9e/servers HTTP/1.1" status: 202 len: 733 time: 0.4643629'; 21:42:42.360 '[instance: a445709b-6ad0-40ec-8860-bec60b6ca0c2] Claim successful'; 21:42:43.044 '[instance: a445709b-6ad0-40ec-8860-bec60b6ca0c2] Creating image'.
Timeline at the slow build: 21:43:27.498 '[instance: a445709b-6ad0-40ec-8860-bec60b6ca0c2] VM Started (Lifecycle Event)'; 21:43:27.561 'VM Paused (Lifecycle Event)'; 21:43:33.752 'VM Resumed (Lifecycle Event)'; 21:43:33.761 'Instance spawned successfully.'; 21:43:33.762 'Took 50.72 seconds to spawn the instance on the hypervisor.'; 21:43:33.901 'Took 51.59 seconds to build instance.'
Timeline after: 21:43:41.514 'DELETE /v2/54fadb412c4e40cdbaed9335e4c35a9e/servers/a445709b-6ad0-40ec-8860-bec60b6ca0c2 HTTP/1.1" status: 204'; 21:43:41.553 '[instance: a445709b-6ad0-40ec-8860-bec60b6ca0c2] Terminating instance'; 21:43:41.771 'Instance destroyed successfully.' The destroy step took 1.02 s, which is normal against a 1.02 s median.
In the all-scope window of 120 s either side of the anchor, the closest lines outside it are 121.2 s before (nova-api GET servers/detail, 200, 0.2647479 s) and 120.5 s after (nova-api GET servers/detail, 200, 0.2609081 s). The window itself held 535 log lines. The request-scoped search returned 11 lines before the anchor and none after it.
The non-VM flagged HTTP lines all fall on 2017-05-17 around 06:25. Examples: POST os-server-external-events took 2.145 s (median 0.095 s) and GET servers/detail with host=cp-1.slowvm1 took 4.164 s (median 0.333 s).
The log lines carry no node value. The 'Took N seconds to build instance' search reports distinct_nodes 0 across its 2066 matches.
Hypothesis: The slow spawns may come from contention on the compute host (for example disk or image I/O while creating or booting the instance). The worst VM's own lines show the log going quiet between 'Creating image' (21:42:43.044) and 'VM Started' (21:43:27.498). Five of the six slow VMs fall in the 2017-05-14 21:08–21:47 stretch. Would confirm: Check for host-level I/O or CPU saturation, or image fetch delays (glance/_base cache), in the 2017-05-14 21:08–21:47 range. Compare per-step timestamps for the other five slow VMs against the worst VM. If 'Creating image' → 'VM Started' is also the long gap there, the cause is in image or disk preparation.
Unknown: The logs don't record which compute node ran each slow VM, so local vs spread across hosts cannot be established.

Unknown: Customer impact, downtime and cost are not in the logs.
Unknown: Whether the VMs were slow in the guest (boot, network) after 'spawned successfully' is not shown.

Compare the gap between 'Creating image' and 'VM Started' with the worst VM's. — This shows whether the delay sits in the same step for all six VMs, as the worst VM's timeline suggests.
Next step: Inspect nova-compute, libvirt and glance image-cache logs and host I/O metrics for 2017-05-14 21:08–21:47 and 2017-05-16 16:49. Include the 2017-05-17 06:25 HTTP slowness on the cp-1.slowvm1 host query. — Flagged bursts cluster in these times (ev-56b1e3c23c). Host metrics would confirm or rule out the contention hypothesis.

Patterns 943, 944 and 945 (invalid operation exception: software, sqrt, int cnvt; node-platform) each had 14 bursts versus 0 previously, 24 log lines and 15 nodes, first seen 2005-11-17 04:22:37.

1. ciod 'Link has been severed' on CioStream socket: a new network/I/O failure pattern that is still recurring at period end. Investigate first. — owner hpc-workloads — 27 bursts (previous period 0, change 27), 10408 log lines, 1024 nodes, 3 weeks active, first seen 2005-11-17; 3466 log lines on 2005-11-26, last line 2005-11-28 10:55:14. — Review the burst start times against job runs and I/O node or network events, and decide whether this is one shared cause or many jobs ending.
2. Kill job timed out, block freed (job or application failure), the most frequent single pattern. — owner node-platform — 34 bursts vs 41 previously (change -7), 48 log lines, 5 weeks active. — Confirm whether the job timeouts cluster on particular blocks or users and why jobs are not terminating in time.
3. rts panic - stopping execution (system software failure), recurring across many nodes and rising. — owner node-platform — 33 bursts vs 27 previously (change 6), 33 nodes, 5 weeks active. — Check the nodes and software versions involved and whether panics follow the same job or event.
4. New invalid operation exception patterns (software, sqrt, int cnvt) that all appeared on 2005-11-17. — owner node-platform — 14 bursts each vs 0 previously, 24 log lines each, 15 nodes, 3 weeks active. — Identify the programs or nodes producing them (top node holds 0.333 of lines) and whether they are one event reported three ways.
5. Node card not fully functional / cannot get assembly information (hardware failure) falling but widespread. — owner cluster-control — 9 bursts each vs 19 previously (change -10), 561 log lines, 456 nodes, 4 weeks active. — Confirm the decline is real and check whether remaining bursts hit the same node cards.
Hypothesis: The ciod 'Link has been severed' bursts may be linked to the invalid operation exception patterns that first appeared on the same day (2005-11-17), for example a shared job or software change. Would confirm: Compare burst start times and the nodes or jobs involved for patterns 968 and 943-945, and check for a software or job change on 2005-11-17.
Hypothesis: The surge of pattern 968 on 2005-11-24 to 2005-11-27 may come from a few large jobs failing on all 1024 nodes rather than a persistent network fault. Would confirm: Look at the job and block identifiers in the 2005-11-24 to 11-27 log lines and whether lines per burst are near-identical across bursts.
Unknown: Root cause of any pattern cannot be established from these logs.
Unknown: Customer impact, downtime and cost are not in the logs.

Next step: Compare patterns 943-945 and 968 timing on 2005-11-17 and review pattern 69 and 261 nodes for repeat offenders. — Pattern 69 rose by 6 bursts to 33, pattern 261 is the most frequent at 34 bursts, and 943-945 are new at 14 bursts each.
Next step: Verify the fall in node card warnings (9 bursts vs 19) and check whether the 456 nodes share node cards. — Pattern 165/166 spread across 456 nodes despite the decline.

sql: WITH now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS lines, count(DISTINCT node) AS nodes, count(DISTINCT date_trunc('week', ts)) AS weeks_active, count(*) FILTER (WHERE (severity IN ('FATAL', 'FAILURE', 'SEVERE', 'ERROR', 'CRITICAL') OR severity IN ('WARN', 'WARNING') OR status >= 500 OR severity IS NULL)) AS problem_lines FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND ts >= '2005-11-01 00:00:00' AND ts < '2005-11-29 00:00:00' AND pattern_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), top_node AS ( SELECT pattern_id, max(n) AS top_node_lines FROM ( SELECT pattern_id, node, count(*) AS n FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND ts >= '2005-11-01 00:00:00' AND ts < '2005-11-29 00:00:00' AND node IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, 2) GROUP BY 1 ), b_now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND start_ts >= '2005-11-01 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2005-11-29 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), b_prev AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts_prev FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND start_ts >= '2005-10-04 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2005-11-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), base AS ( SELECT p.pattern_id, p.template, p.component, coalesce(o.team, 'unowned') AS team, p.severity, now.lines, now.problem_lines, now.nodes, now.weeks_active, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) AS bursts, coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS bursts_prev, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) - coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS change, round(top_node.top_node_lines::DOUBLE / now.lines, 3) AS top_node_share, p.first_ts AS first_seen, p.first_ts >= '2005-11-01 00:00:00' AS new, round(j.p_fault, 3) AS p_fault, round(j.p_dump, 3) AS p_dump, round(j.p_problem, 3) AS p_problem, round(j.p_threat, 3) AS p_threat, j.kind FROM now JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = 'bgl' AND p.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = 'bgl' AND j.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = 'bgl' AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN top_node ON top_node.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_now ON b_now.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_prev ON b_prev.pattern_id = now.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND now.problem_lines > 0 AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 ) SELECT *, count(*) OVER () AS candidates FROM base ORDER BY bursts DESC, nodes DESC, pattern_id LIMIT 15

In 2005-11-01 to 2005-11-29 the most frequent problem patterns were all FATAL: "Kill job timed out" (34 bursts) and "rts panic" (33 bursts), both node-platform. Investigate first the new hpc-workloads pattern "ciod: ... Link has been severed": 27 bursts versus 0 in the previous period, across 1024 nodes.
Scope: Dataset bgl, 2005-11-01 00:00 to 2005-11-29 00:00 (end exclusive); previous period 2005-10-04 to 2005-11-01. Problem patterns with p_problem >= 0.5, ranked by bursts (30-min gap) and by growth. Results are truncated: top 15 of 126 matching patterns for the burst ranking and top 10 for growth. The FATAL weekly trend is limited to the 5 largest groups, which here are hpc-workloads and node-platform. Patterns 45, 46 and 47 (40 bursts each) were excluded because p_problem < 0.5.
Log lines by owning team in the period: node-platform 587242, hpc-workloads 27963, cluster-control 4459, out of 619664 total.
Pattern 968 (ciod: Error reading message prefix on CioStream socket, Link has been severed; owner hpc-workloads) had 27 bursts versus 0 in the previous period (change 27), 10408 log lines on 1024 nodes, active in 3 weeks. It was first seen 2005-11-17 05:33:24.623263.
Daily log lines for pattern 968: 1008 on 2005-11-17, 0 on both 2005-11-19 and 2005-11-20, 2047 on 2005-11-24, 3466 on 2005-11-26, 512 on 2005-11-28. The last line in the period was 2005-11-28 10:55:14.478042.
Across the whole corpus, pattern 968 has 26546 matching log lines on 1024 distinct nodes, from 2005-11-17 05:33:24.623263 to 2006-01-03 11:56:38.877831.
Pattern 261 (Kill job timed out. Block freed.; node-platform) had 34 bursts versus 41 previously (change -7), 48 log lines, active in 5 weeks.
Pattern 69 (rts panic! - stopping execution; node-platform) had 33 bursts versus 27 previously (change 6), 45 log lines on 33 nodes, active in 5 weeks.
Patterns 943, 944 and 945 (invalid operation exception: software, sqrt, int cnvt; node-platform) each had 14 bursts versus 0 previously, 24 log lines on 15 nodes, active in 3 weeks. All three were first seen on 2005-11-17 at 04:22:37.
Patterns 165 (Node card is not fully functional) and 166 (Can not get assembly information for node card), owner cluster-control, each had 9 bursts versus 19 previously (change -10), 561 log lines on 456 nodes, active in 4 weeks.
Pattern 33 (machine check interrupt; node-platform) had 17 bursts versus 30 previously (change -13), 18 log lines on 18 nodes.
FATAL log lines per week (weeks starting 2005-10-31, 11-07, 11-14, 11-21, 11-28): hpc-workloads 5680, 2232, 5631, 13892, 528; node-platform 269, 4540, 7411, 1489, 1129. FATAL total in the period was 42801.
1. Investigate first: new ciod "Link has been severed" errors on CioStream sockets, the largest growth and widest spread of any problem pattern this period. — owner hpc-workloads — 27 bursts vs 0 previous (change 27); 10408 log lines; 1024 nodes; 3 weeks active; first seen 2005-11-17 05:33:24.623263; 3466 log lines on 2005-11-26. — Check whether the severed links trace to a shared I/O or network path, and why the lines continue after the period (corpus last line 2006-01-03).
2. Kill job timed out. Block freed. is the most frequent problem pattern by bursts, but it is declining. — owner node-platform — 34 bursts vs 41 previous (change -7); 48 log lines; 5 weeks active. — Review the timed-out jobs and why blocks were not freed in time; it recurs every week of the period.
3. rts panic! - stopping execution recurs on many nodes and is rising. — owner node-platform — 33 bursts vs 27 previous (change 6); 45 log lines; 33 nodes; 5 weeks active. — Check whether the panics cluster by rack or midplane and compare against the machine check pattern.
4. New invalid operation exception patterns (software, sqrt, int cnvt) appearing together from 2005-11-17. — owner node-platform — Each 14 bursts vs 0 previous (change 14); 24 log lines; 15 nodes; 3 weeks active. — Check which jobs or nodes these hit and whether they relate to the ciod errors that began the same day.
5. Node card is not fully functional and Can not get assembly information for node card are the cluster-control pattern pair, and both are declining. — owner cluster-control — 9 bursts each vs 19 previous (change -10); 561 log lines; 456 nodes; 4 weeks active. — Confirm that the decline reflects real recovery and not reduced logging.
Hypothesis: The ciod link-severed errors and the new invalid-operation exceptions may share a trigger, because both first appear on 2005-11-17 (04:22:37 and 05:33:24). Would confirm: Run precursors or a timeline for pattern 968 around 2005-11-17 04:00 to 06:00 and see whether patterns 943-945 precede it on the same nodes.
Hypothesis: The ciod severed links may come from a network or I/O path problem and not from individual compute nodes, since the lines span 1024 nodes with a top-node share of 0.001. Would confirm: Group pattern 968 by location, rack and the peer address in the message, and check I/O node logs.
Unknown: Root cause of any pattern cannot be established from these logs.
Unknown: Customer impact, job loss, downtime and cost are not in the logs.
Unknown: The results are truncated to the top 15 of 126 problem patterns, so less frequent patterns are not covered.
Unknown: Pattern 261 shows nodes = 0 in the results; this is unexplained.
Next step: Open an investigation on pattern 968 (ciod Link has been severed): break it down by location and peer address, and review the daily bursts on 2005-11-24 to 2005-11-26. — New this period: 27 bursts vs 0 previous, 1024 nodes, 10408 log lines, with a peak of 3466 log lines on 2005-11-26.
Next step: Run a precursors/timeline check on patterns 943-945 and 968 around 2005-11-17, the day both groups were first seen. — Both groups first appear on the same morning, 2005-11-17, which could indicate a common trigger.
Next step: Review the recurring panics and job-timeout patterns (69 and 261) by rack and week. — They have the highest burst counts (33 and 34) and were active in 5 weeks each.

Fleet-wide, not one bad node: in 2005-10-01 to 2005-11-01 the message appeared in 46 log lines on 38 distinct nodes, and no node had more than 2 lines.
Scope: Dataset bgl, 2005-10-01 00:00:00 to 2005-11-01 00:00:00 (previous period for burst change: 2005-08-31 to 2005-10-01). Filter: the phrase 'rts panic! - stopping execution' (pattern_id 69, component KERNEL). The sample search shows 5 of 46 rows and the per-node and per-location breakdowns list only the top 5 and top 10 groups, so they are truncated. Totals, the daily trend and the pattern ranking are not affected. The ranking is truncated to 10 of 40 KERNEL problem patterns.
The phrase matched 46 log lines on 38 distinct nodes between 2005-10-01 11:02:59.249894 and 2005-10-31 20:44:07.437222.
The most affected nodes each had only 2 log lines (for example R02-M1-N6-C:J12-U01, R10-M0-NE-C:J05-U01 and R30-M1-NF-C:J13-U01), out of 38 nodes in total.
The top node accounts for a top_node_share of 0.043 of the pattern's log lines.
The pattern had 33 bursts in the period against 51 in the previous period (change -18), was active in 6 weeks, and is rated FATAL with p_problem 0.912.
The first 5 sample lines come from 5 different nodes: R04-M0-N3-C:J17-U11, R52-M0-NB-C:J04-U01, R22-M0-NA-C:J11-U01, R21-M0-NB-C:J07-U01 and R62-M0-N4-C:J13-U01.
Daily log lines peaked at 14 on 2005-10-23; 2005-10-22 had 3 and 2005-10-24 had 0. Many days had 0 lines, for example 2005-10-05 to 2005-10-11.
Across the whole history of this pattern (2005-06-05 to 2006-01-03) it has 3983 log lines, 236 bursts and 3394 nodes, owned by node-platform.
1. 'rts panic! - stopping execution': FATAL kernel panic spread across many nodes. Investigate first because it is widespread across the fleet and not tied to one node, so replacing a single node will not fix it. — owner node-platform — 46 log lines, 38 nodes, 33 bursts (previous period 51, change -18), 6 weeks active, top_node_share 0.043, peak of 14 log lines on 2005-10-23. — Check what the 38 nodes share (software build, job type, rack or midplane) and what precedes the panic on the 2005-10-23 spike.
2. 'Kill job <N> timed out. Block freed.' is the KERNEL problem pattern with the most bursts and is rising. — owner node-platform — 44 bursts (previous period 29, change 15), 47 log lines, 6 weeks active. — Review the jobs and blocks involved and whether the rise relates to the panics.
3. 'machine check interrupt' (hardware failure) recurs on many nodes. — owner node-platform — 34 bursts (previous period 38, change -4), 37 log lines, 34 nodes, 6 weeks active. — Check whether the affected nodes overlap with the rts panic nodes.
Hypothesis: The panics may come from a shared software or service cause (such as a common kernel/runtime build or job type) rather than from per-node hardware, since they are spread thinly across 38 nodes. Would confirm: Compare the software version, job and block at each panic time, and check whether the 14 log lines on 2005-10-23 share a job or rack.
Hypothesis: The spike on 2005-10-23 may be one correlated event hitting many nodes at once. Would confirm: List the nodes and timestamps for 2005-10-23 and check whether they fall within one burst or one job/block.
Unknown: The root cause is not established by these logs.
Unknown: Whether the 38 nodes share a rack, midplane, job or software version was not examined; only the sample's first 5 nodes were listed.
Unknown: Customer impact, downtime and cost are not in the logs.
Unknown: Node counts for the 'Kill job' pattern show 0 in the ranking, so its spread is unknown.
Next step: Run the facet/count_by on rack and midplane for pattern 69 in October 2005, and list the log lines for 2005-10-23. — Of the 46 log lines, 14 fall on 2005-10-23, and the 38 nodes need to be grouped to find a common factor.
Next step: Run the precursors check for pattern_id 69 to see what is logged just before the panics. — This could separate a software cause from hardware errors such as the 34 bursts of 'machine check interrupt'.
Next step: Correlate the 'Kill job timed out' bursts (44) with the rts panic bursts (33) by time. — Both rank highly in KERNEL problems, and the job timeouts rose by 15 bursts while panics fell by 18.

rows.title: Blue Gene/L supercomputer RAS logs (LLNL)
rows.description: Loghub BGL: reliability/availability/serviceability events of the Blue Gene/L supercomputer, 2005-06-03 to 2006-01-04 (214 days). Location = rack/midplane/node (R02-M1-N0-C:J12-U11: rack R02, midplane M1, node card N0, C = compute / I = I/O card). Components KERNEL, APP, MMCS, ... Alert labels exist for evaluation only.

rows.location_meaning: rack/midplane/node (first level = a whole rack, two levels = a midplane)

sql: WITH now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS lines, count(DISTINCT node) AS nodes, count(DISTINCT date_trunc('week', ts)) AS weeks_active, count(*) FILTER (WHERE (severity IN ('FATAL', 'FAILURE', 'SEVERE', 'ERROR', 'CRITICAL') OR severity IN ('WARN', 'WARNING') OR status >= 500 OR severity IS NULL)) AS problem_lines FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND ts >= '2005-06-03 00:00:00' AND ts < '2006-01-05 00:00:00' AND pattern_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), top_node AS ( SELECT pattern_id, max(n) AS top_node_lines FROM ( SELECT pattern_id, node, count(*) AS n FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND ts >= '2005-06-03 00:00:00' AND ts < '2006-01-05 00:00:00' AND node IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, 2) GROUP BY 1 ), b_now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND start_ts >= '2005-06-03 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2006-01-05 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), b_prev AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts_prev FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND start_ts >= '2004-10-30 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2005-06-03 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), base AS ( SELECT p.pattern_id, p.template, p.component, coalesce(o.team, 'unowned') AS team, p.severity, now.lines, now.problem_lines, now.nodes, now.weeks_active, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) AS bursts, coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS bursts_prev, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) - coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS change, round(top_node.top_node_lines::DOUBLE / now.lines, 3) AS top_node_share, p.first_ts AS first_seen, p.first_ts >= '2005-06-03 00:00:00' AS new, round(j.p_fault, 3) AS p_fault, round(j.p_dump, 3) AS p_dump, round(j.p_problem, 3) AS p_problem, round(j.p_threat, 3) AS p_threat, j.kind FROM now JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = 'bgl' AND p.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = 'bgl' AND j.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = 'bgl' AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN top_node ON top_node.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_now ON b_now.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_prev ON b_prev.pattern_id = now.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND now.problem_lines > 0 AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 AND p.component = 'KERNEL' ) SELECT *, count(*) OVER () AS candidates FROM base ORDER BY bursts DESC, nodes DESC, pattern_id LIMIT 10

Scope: Dataset bgl, period 2005-10-01 to 2005-11-01 versus previous period 2005-08-31 to 2005-10-01 (used as 'September'). Filter: problem patterns with p_problem >= 0.5, ranked by change in bursts. Results truncated: 15 of 86 candidates shown, so the ranking covers the top 15 by growth only.
Pattern 261 'Kill job <N> timed out. Block freed.' (KERNEL, node-platform, FATAL) had 44 bursts against 29 in the previous period, a change of 15, with 47 log lines and activity in 6 weeks.
Pattern 93 'machine check interrupt (bit=<N>): L<N> major internal error' (node-platform) had 10 bursts against 5 (change 5), on 8 nodes, active in 5 weeks.
Pattern 467 'Microloader Assertion' (node-platform, FATAL) had 2 bursts against 0 previously, with 18 log lines on 18 nodes, active in 2 weeks. Its first_seen is 2005-08-03 16:38:58.627303.
Patterns 120, 122, 123, 124, 125, 126, 135, 153, 154, 158 and 160 (uncorrectable error / parity error / DDR register patterns, node-platform) each had 4 bursts against 2 (change 2), on 4 nodes, active in 4 weeks, with a top-node share of 0.25.
Pattern 318 'NodeCard is not fully functional' (HARDWARE, node-platform, SEVERE) had 3 bursts against 1 (change 2), on 1 node, active in 1 week, with a top-node share of 1.0.
Some high-volume patterns fell: pattern 69 'rts panic! - stopping execution' went from 51 to 33 bursts (change -18), pattern 33 'machine check interrupt' from 38 to 34 (change -4), and the cluster-control DISCOVERY patterns 165 and 166 went from 24 to 20 (change -4) and from 23 to 20 (change -3) bursts.

new.text:
In October 2005 the recurring problems that increased most in bursts versus the previous period were all in KERNEL and HARDWARE components owned by node-platform. Investigate first the job-kill timeout pattern 261 ("Kill job <N> timed out. Block freed."), which went from 29 bursts to 44, a change of 15.
Scope: Dataset bgl. Period 2005-10-01 to 2005-11-01, compared with the previous period 2005-08-31 to 2005-10-01. Filter: problem patterns only (p_problem >= 0.5), ranked by change in bursts. Results are truncated: 15 of 86 candidate patterns shown, and many patterns tie at a change of 2. Weekly heatmap and trend cover 2005-09-01 to 2005-11-01, with calendar weeks that straddle month edges.
Pattern 261 "Kill job <N> timed out. Block freed." (KERNEL, node-platform, severity FATAL) had 44 bursts in the period versus 29 in the previous period, a change of 15. It had 47 log lines and was active in 6 weeks.
Pattern 261 weekly log lines: 4 (week of 2005-08-29), 10, 2, 4, 8, 6, 7, then 20 (week of 2005-10-17), 10 (week of 2005-10-24) and 2 (week of 2005-10-31).
Pattern 93 "machine check interrupt (bit=<N>): L<N> major internal error" (KERNEL, node-platform, FATAL) had 10 bursts versus 5 previously, a change of 5, on 8 nodes and active in 5 weeks.
Patterns 120, 122, 123, 124, 125, 126, 135, 153, 154, 158 and 160 (uncorrectable or parity errors and DDR registers, KERNEL, node-platform, FATAL) each had 4 bursts versus 2 previously, a change of 2, on 4 nodes and active in 4 weeks.
Pattern 467 "Microloader Assertion" (KERNEL, node-platform, FATAL) had 2 bursts versus 0 previously, on 18 nodes in 2 weeks. First seen 2005-08-03 16:38:58.627303.
Pattern 318 "NodeCard is not fully functional" (HARDWARE, node-platform, SEVERE) had 3 bursts versus 1 previously, a change of 2, all on 1 node in 1 week.
Of 345 problem-pattern bursts in October, node-platform owned 251, cluster-control 51 and hpc-workloads 43.
Weekly problem-pattern bursts for node-platform were 61, 32, 55 and 90 for the weeks of 2005-09-05 to 2005-09-26, and 52, 34, 61, 65 and 8 for the weeks of 2005-10-03 to 2005-10-31. hpc-workloads had 19, 10, 14 and 17 in the September weeks and 7, 10, 14, 8 and 0 in the October weeks.
58 problem patterns were first seen in October. The top ones by bursts were node-platform ciod core-file patterns such as 745 (5 bursts, 2560 log lines, 512 nodes) and 773 (5 bursts, 89 log lines, 33 nodes), plus hpc-workloads ciod load errors.
FATAL log lines in October totalled 42589: hpc-workloads 36295, node-platform 6293, cluster-control 1.
1. Investigate first: job-kill timeouts ("Kill job <N> timed out. Block freed.") are recurring more often. It has the largest increase in bursts among the patterns shown, is FATAL, and has been active for 6 weeks. — owner node-platform — 44 bursts vs 29 previously (change 15); 47 log lines; 6 weeks active; 20 log lines in the week of 2005-10-17. — Pull the log context for the bursts in the week of 2005-10-17 and check whether they cluster on the same jobs, blocks or midplanes.
2. Machine check interrupt (L<N> major internal error), a FATAL hardware failure pattern, is recurring about twice as often. — owner node-platform — 10 bursts vs 5 previously (change 5); 8 nodes; 5 weeks active. — Check the 8 affected nodes for shared hardware, such as the same rack or midplane, and for repeat offenders.
3. A family of FATAL memory and parity error patterns (uncorrectable errors, EDRAM, DDR, read queue) each doubled in bursts. — owner node-platform — Each pattern: 4 bursts vs 2 previously (change 2); 4 nodes; 4 weeks active. Pattern IDs 120, 122, 123, 124, 125, 126, 135, 153, 154, 158 and 160. — Check whether these patterns fire together on the same 4 nodes. If so, treat them as one memory-fault investigation rather than separate problems.
4. Microloader Assertion (FATAL) is recurring across many nodes. — owner node-platform — 2 bursts vs 0 previously (change 2); 18 nodes; 2 weeks active. — Review the assertion lines across the 18 nodes for a common boot, firmware or software version.
5. NodeCard is not fully functional (SEVERE) recurred on a single node. — owner node-platform — 3 bursts vs 1 previously (change 2); 1 node; 1 week active. — Check the state of that node card and whether it was serviced.
Hypothesis: The memory and parity error patterns may come from one underlying fault event that logs several message types together, because they share identical counts (4 bursts, 4 nodes, 4 weeks). Would confirm: Compare the timestamps and nodes of the bursts across these patterns. If they co-occur in the same bursts and nodes, it is one fault signature.
Hypothesis: The rise in Kill job timeouts may be linked to the large jobs that started in October, some of which generated core files. Would confirm: Correlate the timeout bursts in the week of 2005-10-17 with the job IDs and ciod core-file or load-error lines from the same hours.
Unknown: Root cause of every pattern is not established by these logs.
Unknown: Customer impact, downtime and cost are not in the logs.
Unknown: A full September-versus-October total per team was not computed; the weekly heatmap uses calendar weeks that straddle the month boundaries.
Unknown: The ranking is truncated (15 of 86 candidates) and many patterns tie at a change of 2, so other patterns with the same change may exist.
Unknown: Patterns with p_problem below 0.5 were excluded, including KERNEL patterns 32, 34 and 35 at 55 to 58 bursts each in October.
Unknown: The 36295 hpc-workloads FATAL log lines in October have no previous-period comparison here, so whether they got worse is unknown.
Unknown: Pattern 261 shows nodes = 0 in the result, so the affected nodes are not known.
Next step: Open the log context around the pattern 261 bursts in the week of 2005-10-17 and list the job IDs, blocks and nodes involved. — Pattern 261 has the largest increase in bursts (44 vs 29) and a peak of 20 log lines in that week.
Next step: Check hardware status and service history for the 8 nodes with pattern 93 and the 4 nodes with the memory/parity patterns. — Both groups of FATAL hardware patterns roughly doubled in bursts versus the previous period.
Next step: Run a September-versus-October comparison per team and per pattern for hpc-workloads FATAL ciod load errors. — They account for 36295 FATAL log lines in October but their growth was not measured here.
Next step: Re-run the growth ranking with a higher limit (up to 50) to see all patterns tied at a change of 2. — Only 15 of 86 candidates were shown, so other patterns that got worse may be missing.

sql: WITH now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS lines, count(DISTINCT node) AS nodes, count(DISTINCT date_trunc('week', ts)) AS weeks_active, count(*) FILTER (WHERE (severity IN ('FATAL', 'FAILURE', 'SEVERE', 'ERROR', 'CRITICAL') OR severity IN ('WARN', 'WARNING') OR status >= 500 OR severity IS NULL)) AS problem_lines FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND ts >= '2005-10-01 00:00:00' AND ts < '2005-11-01 00:00:00' AND pattern_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), top_node AS ( SELECT pattern_id, max(n) AS top_node_lines FROM ( SELECT pattern_id, node, count(*) AS n FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND ts >= '2005-10-01 00:00:00' AND ts < '2005-11-01 00:00:00' AND node IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, 2) GROUP BY 1 ), b_now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND start_ts >= '2005-10-01 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2005-11-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), b_prev AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts_prev FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND start_ts >= '2005-08-31 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2005-10-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), base AS ( SELECT p.pattern_id, p.template, p.component, coalesce(o.team, 'unowned') AS team, p.severity, now.lines, now.problem_lines, now.nodes, now.weeks_active, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) AS bursts, coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS bursts_prev, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) - coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS change, round(top_node.top_node_lines::DOUBLE / now.lines, 3) AS top_node_share, p.first_ts AS first_seen, p.first_ts >= '2005-10-01 00:00:00' AS new, round(j.p_fault, 3) AS p_fault, round(j.p_dump, 3) AS p_dump, round(j.p_problem, 3) AS p_problem, round(j.p_threat, 3) AS p_threat, j.kind FROM now JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = 'bgl' AND p.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = 'bgl' AND j.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = 'bgl' AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN top_node ON top_node.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_now ON b_now.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_prev ON b_prev.pattern_id = now.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND now.problem_lines > 0 AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 ), inputs AS ( SELECT *, round(weeks_active::DOUBLE / 6, 3) AS persistence, round(problem_lines::DOUBLE / lines, 3) AS problem_share, p_problem AS severity_input FROM base ), ranked AS ( SELECT *, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY bursts) AS pr_frequency, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY change) AS pr_trend, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY nodes) AS pr_spread, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY persistence) AS pr_persistence, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY severity_input) AS pr_severity FROM inputs ) SELECT *, round(100 * (0.3 * pr_frequency + 0.2 * pr_trend + 0.25 * pr_spread + 0.15 * pr_persistence + 0.1 * pr_severity), 1) AS score FROM ranked ORDER BY score DESC, bursts DESC, pattern_id

coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS change, round(top_node.top_node_lines::DOUBLE / now.lines, 3) AS top_node_share, p.first_ts AS first_seen, p.first_ts >= '2005-10-01 00:00:00' AS new, round(j.p_fault, 3) AS p_fault, round(j.p_dump, 3) AS p_dump, round(j.p_problem, 3) AS p_problem, round(j.p_threat, 3) AS p_threat, j.kind FROM now JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = 'bgl' AND p.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = 'bgl' AND j.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = 'bgl' AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN top_node ON top_node.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_now ON b_now.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_prev ON b_prev.pattern_id = now.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND now.problem_lines > 0 AND coalesce(j.p_problem, 0) < 0.5 ) SELECT pattern_id, template, component, team, bursts, lines, nodes, p_problem, kind FROM base ORDER BY bursts DESC, pattern_id LIMIT 3

sql: SELECT s.b AS bucket_start, count(x.t) AS bursts FROM generate_series(date_trunc('week', TIMESTAMP '2005-09-01 00:00:00'), TIMESTAMP '2005-10-01 00:00:00', interval '7 days') s(b) LEFT JOIN (SELECT b.start_ts AS t FROM bursts b JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = b.dataset AND p.pattern_id = b.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = p.dataset AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = p.dataset AND j.pattern_id = p.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 AND p.problem_lines > 0 AND b.dataset = 'bgl' AND b.start_ts >= '2005-09-01 00:00:00' AND b.start_ts < '2005-10-01 00:00:00') x ON date_trunc('week', x.t) = s.b GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT team, round(regr_slope(n, i), 3) AS slope, sum(n) AS bursts FROM (SELECT t.team, s.i, count(x.t) AS n FROM (SELECT row_number() OVER (ORDER BY b) - 1 AS i, b FROM generate_series(date_trunc('week', TIMESTAMP '2005-11-01 00:00:00'), TIMESTAMP '2005-11-29 00:00:00', interval '7 days') s(b)) s CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT coalesce(o.team, 'unowned') AS team FROM bursts b JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = b.dataset AND p.pattern_id = b.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = p.dataset AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = p.dataset AND j.pattern_id = p.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 AND p.problem_lines > 0 AND b.dataset = 'bgl' AND b.start_ts >= '2005-11-01 00:00:00' AND b.start_ts < '2005-11-29 00:00:00') t LEFT JOIN (SELECT b.start_ts AS t, coalesce(o.team, 'unowned') AS team FROM bursts b JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = b.dataset AND p.pattern_id = b.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = p.dataset AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = p.dataset AND j.pattern_id = p.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 AND p.problem_lines > 0 AND b.dataset = 'bgl' AND b.start_ts >= '2005-11-01 00:00:00' AND b.start_ts < '2005-11-29 00:00:00') x ON date_trunc('week', x.t) = s.b AND x.team = t.team GROUP BY 1, 2) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY bursts DESC

sql: WITH now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS lines, count(DISTINCT node) AS nodes, count(DISTINCT date_trunc('week', ts)) AS weeks_active, count(*) FILTER (WHERE (severity IN ('FATAL', 'FAILURE', 'SEVERE', 'ERROR', 'CRITICAL') OR severity IN ('WARN', 'WARNING') OR status >= 500 OR severity IS NULL)) AS problem_lines FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND ts >= '2005-11-01 00:00:00' AND ts < '2005-11-29 00:00:00' AND pattern_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), top_node AS ( SELECT pattern_id, max(n) AS top_node_lines FROM ( SELECT pattern_id, node, count(*) AS n FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND ts >= '2005-11-01 00:00:00' AND ts < '2005-11-29 00:00:00' AND node IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, 2) GROUP BY 1 ), b_now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND start_ts >= '2005-11-01 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2005-11-29 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), b_prev AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts_prev FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND start_ts >= '2005-10-04 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2005-11-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), base AS ( SELECT p.pattern_id, p.template, p.component, coalesce(o.team, 'unowned') AS team, p.severity, now.lines, now.problem_lines, now.nodes, now.weeks_active, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) AS bursts, coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS bursts_prev, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) - Scope: Dataset bgl, 2005-09-01 to 2005-11-29 (14 weeks), compared with the previous period 2005-06-04 to 2005-09-01. Problem patterns only (judged p_problem >= 0.5). The priority table is truncated (10 shown of 272 matches). The weekly trend results are not truncated.
node-platform had 775 bursts in the period against 615 in the previous period (change 160) across 63 problem patterns.
hpc-workloads had 245 bursts in the period against 30 in the previous period (change 215) across 168 problem patterns.
cluster-control had 178 bursts in the period against 180 in the previous period (change -2) across 41 problem patterns.
Weekly FATAL log lines for node-platform fell from 9996 (week of 2005-09-05) to 409 (week of 2005-10-31), then rose to 4540 (week of 2005-11-07) and 7411 (week of 2005-11-14).
Weekly FATAL log lines for hpc-workloads were 25568 in the week of 2005-09-19 and 13892 in the week of 2005-11-21, with 2232 in the week of 2005-11-07 in between.

Between 2015-07-29 and 2015-08-26 the most recurring problem patterns were in client-connectivity ("caught end of stream exception", 18 bursts) and coordination-platform (election-channel and learner/follower connection failures). Investigate first the coordination-platform pattern "Cannot open channel to <N> at election address": it was active in 5 weeks and was still logging on 2015-08-25.
Scope: Dataset zookeeper, 2015-07-29 00:00 to 2015-08-26 00:00, compared with the previous period 2015-07-01 to 2015-07-29. Problem patterns only (p_problem >= 0.5): 11 matches, the burst-ranked list is not truncated, the growth-ranked list shows 10 of 11. Zookeeper logs no node or host, so nodes = 0 means spread unknown. The log-line search for pattern 200018 is a 2-row sample of 2,584 matches.
Pattern 200062 "caught end of stream exception" (client-connectivity, WARN) had 18 bursts versus 0 in the previous period, 1670 log lines, active in 3 weeks.
Pattern 200018 "Cannot open channel to <N> at election address" (coordination-platform, WARN) had 8 bursts versus 0 in the previous period, 2584 log lines, active in 5 weeks.
Pattern 200018 log lines per day: 28 on 2015-07-29, 71 on 2015-07-30, 36 on 2015-07-31, then at most 14 per day until 2015-08-23, then 1039 on 2015-08-24 and 1378 on 2015-08-25.
The latest sampled pattern 200018 lines are from 2015-08-25 11:23:57, component QuorumCnxManager, location WorkerSender[myid=3], body "Cannot open channel to 2 at election address /10.10.34.12:3888".
WARN log lines for coordination-platform per week (week starting): 42304 on 2015-07-27, 16 on 2015-08-03, 19 on 2015-08-10, 27 on 2015-08-17, 2443 on 2015-08-24.
WARN log lines for client-connectivity per week (week starting): 2793 on 2015-07-27, 0 on 2015-08-03, 355 on 2015-08-10, 550 on 2015-08-17, 0 on 2015-08-24.
Pattern 200062 log lines per day: 250 on 2015-07-29, 742 on 2015-07-30, 371 on 2015-07-31, 132 on 2015-08-10, 171 on 2015-08-20; last line 2015-08-21 15:55:06.
Pattern 200048 "Unexpected exception causing shutdown while sock still open" (LearnerHandler, coordination-platform, ERROR) had 7 bursts versus 0 before, 590 log lines, active in 2 weeks, p_problem 0.903.
Pattern 200050 "Connection broken for id <HEX>, my id = <N>" (coordination-platform) had 1 burst and 10356 log lines, active in 1 week.
Of 74380 log lines in the period, coordination-platform owns 59036, client-connectivity 15060 and storage-persistence 284.
Pattern 200055 "Connection request from old client" (client-connectivity) had 14 bursts and 1861 log lines but was excluded as a problem (p_problem 0.15, kind "not a problem").
1. Investigate first: quorum election channel cannot be opened ("Cannot open channel to <N> at election address"); still logging on 2015-08-25. — owner coordination-platform — 8 bursts (previous period 0, change 8), 2584 log lines, active in 5 weeks (the longest of the listed problems), 1039 log lines on 2015-08-24 and 1378 on 2015-08-25; nodes 0 (spread unknown). — Check the election-port connectivity and state of the peer named in the latest lines (id 2, 10.10.34.12:3888) around 2015-08-24 to 2015-08-25, and what the ensemble did at that time.
2. Client connections ending unexpectedly ("caught end of stream exception"), the most frequent burst pattern. — owner client-connectivity — 18 bursts (previous period 0, change 18), 1670 log lines, active in 3 weeks; last seen 2015-08-21; p_problem 0.551, the lowest among the listed patterns. — Check which clients or sessions drop (days with 742 log lines on 2015-07-30, 132 on 2015-08-10, 171 on 2015-08-20) and decide whether these are normal client disconnects or a real fault.
3. Learner handler shutting down with an unexpected exception while the socket is still open (ERROR). — owner coordination-platform — 7 bursts (previous period 0, change 7), 590 log lines, active in 2 weeks, p_problem 0.903 (highest among the listed patterns). — Review the exception details and the surrounding follower/leader lines to see whether this shares a trigger with the election failures.
4. Quorum receive-worker connection broken ("Connection broken for id <HEX>"): a single large burst. — owner coordination-platform — 1 burst (previous period 0), 10356 log lines, active in 1 week; first seen 2015-07-29 19:04:02. — Treat as one event: establish what happened from 2015-07-29 19:04 and whether it matches the first-week WARN volume of 42304 log lines.
Hypothesis: The recent election-channel warnings may come from one peer (id 2 at 10.10.34.12:3888) being down or unreachable from the node with myid=3, rather than from the whole ensemble. Would confirm: Check whether the id 2 server process was running and reachable on port 3888 on 2015-08-24 to 2015-08-25, and whether other peers log the same failure.
Hypothesis: The election-channel, connection-broken and learner-shutdown patterns may be symptoms of the same network or restart event. Would confirm: Line up the timestamps of patterns 200018, 200050 and 200048 for the bursts and see whether they start together.
Unknown: Root cause is not established by these logs.
Unknown: Which nodes or hosts were affected is unknown, because zookeeper logs no node (nodes = 0).
Unknown: Customer impact, downtime and cost are not in the logs.
Unknown: Whether the 2015-08-24 to 2015-08-25 surge of pattern 200018 had ended by the end of the period is not shown; the last line seen is 2015-08-25 11:23:57.
Next step: Inspect the 2015-08-24 to 2015-08-25 window for pattern 200018 and the surrounding lines, plus the state of the peer named in the latest sampled lines. — The pattern has 8 bursts, was active in 5 weeks, and reached 1039 and 1378 log lines per day at the end of the period.
Next step: Compare the timing of patterns 200048 and 200050 with 200018 to see whether they share a trigger. — The three coordination-platform patterns cover 590, 10356 and 2584 log lines, and all are new versus the previous period.
Next step: Sample client sessions behind "caught end of stream exception" and decide if it is normal client churn or a fault. — It has the most bursts (18) but the lowest p_problem (0.551), and was last seen 2015-08-21.

coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS change, round(top_node.top_node_lines::DOUBLE / now.lines, 3) AS top_node_share, p.first_ts AS first_seen, p.first_ts >= '2015-07-29 00:00:00' AS new, round(j.p_fault, 3) AS p_fault, round(j.p_dump, 3) AS p_dump, round(j.p_problem, 3) AS p_problem, round(j.p_threat, 3) AS p_threat, j.kind FROM now JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = 'zookeeper' AND p.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = 'zookeeper' AND j.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = 'zookeeper' AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN top_node ON top_node.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_now ON b_now.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_prev ON b_prev.pattern_id = now.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND now.problem_lines > 0 AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 ) SELECT *, count(*) OVER () AS candidates FROM base ORDER BY bursts DESC, nodes DESC, pattern_id LIMIT 15

facts.statement: There were 1345 problem bursts in the period: 1205 for web-platform (component httpd) and 140 for app-integration (mod_jk 71, jk2_init() 69).

Team roll-up: web-platform has 17 problem patterns, 1205 bursts (previous period 1334, change -129) and 7690 log lines. app-integration has 2 problem patterns, 140 bursts (previous period 214, change -74) and 2038 log lines.
Weekly problem bursts are rated 'worsening': the first-half mean is 67.29 and the second-half mean is 124.86 (slope 5.312). web-platform slope is 6.38; app-integration slope is -1.068.
Weekly problem bursts peaked at 168 in the week of 2006-01-16 and were 148 in each of the weeks of 2006-02-06, 2006-02-13 and 2006-02-20.
No problem patterns were first seen in this period (0 matches), so the load comes from patterns already known before 2005-12-01.

ranked.problem: 'script not found or unable to stat' (httpd): requests for scripts that cannot be found or accessed
ranked.basis: score 88.9; 127 bursts vs 32 in the previous period (change 95); 3674 log lines; active in 10 of 14 weeks
ranked.action: Decide whether web-platform gets time this cycle to find and fix the cause, since this is the fastest-growing top pattern.

ranked.problem: jk2_init() 'Can't find child in scoreboard': a persistent mod_jk/Apache integration fault
ranked.basis: score 86.8; 69 bursts vs 54 in the previous period (change 15); 415 log lines; active in 13 of 14 weeks
ranked.action: Decide whether app-integration should treat this as a standing defect, since it appeared in nearly every week, and assign an owner to resolve it.

ranked.problem: 'config.update(): Can't create worker.jni:onStartup' (httpd), part of a group of similar worker.jni/channel.jni startup errors
ranked.basis: score 85.0; 11 bursts vs 16 in the previous period (change -5); 11 log lines; active in 9 of 14 weeks
ranked.action: Ask web-platform to fix the jni worker configuration once, because several sibling patterns share the same counts (11 bursts each).

hypotheses.statement: The rise in 'script not found' bursts may come from missing or moved scripts after a deployment, or from automated clients requesting non-existent paths.
hypotheses.would_confirm: Check the requested paths and client IPs in the raw lines, and compare with deployment dates from January 2006.

hypotheses.statement: The identical counts across the worker.jni and channel.jni patterns may indicate a single underlying configuration fault that logs several messages together.
hypotheses.would_confirm: Check whether these patterns' bursts start at the same timestamps.

unknowns: Cost, downtime and customer impact are not in these logs.
Root cause is not established by these logs.
Which host or node is affected is unknown, because Apache logs carry no node field.
The previous-period comparison shows fewer bursts for both teams, while the weekly trend within the period is worsening. The logs do not explain the difference.

next_steps.action: Have web-platform review the top 'script not found' paths and clients from January through February 2006.
next_steps.why: Pattern 300042 has 127 bursts, up 95 from the previous period, and leads the ranking.

next_steps.action: Ask app-integration to investigate the jk2_init() scoreboard error and report back with a cause.
next_steps.why: The pattern was active in 13 of 14 weeks with 69 bursts.

next_steps.action: Review problem-burst trend again after the first two actions, using the same 14-week window.
next_steps.why: Weekly bursts were rated worsening, with a second-half mean of 124.86 against 67.29 in the first half.

coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS change, round(top_node.top_node_lines::DOUBLE / now.lines, 3) AS top_node_share, p.first_ts AS first_seen, p.first_ts >= '2005-12-01 00:00:00' AS new, round(j.p_fault, 3) AS p_fault, round(j.p_dump, 3) AS p_dump, round(j.p_problem, 3) AS p_problem, round(j.p_threat, 3) AS p_threat, j.kind FROM now JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = 'apache' AND p.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = 'apache' AND j.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = 'apache' AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN top_node ON top_node.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_now ON b_now.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_prev ON b_prev.pattern_id = now.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND now.problem_lines > 0 AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 ), inputs AS ( SELECT *, round(weeks_active::DOUBLE / 14, 3) AS persistence, round(problem_lines::DOUBLE / lines, 3) AS problem_share, p_problem AS severity_input FROM base ), ranked AS ( SELECT *, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY bursts) AS pr_frequency, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY change) AS pr_trend, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY nodes) AS pr_spread, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY persistence) AS pr_persistence, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY severity_input) AS pr_severity FROM inputs ) SELECT *, round(100 * (0.3 * pr_frequency + 0.2 * pr_trend + 0.25 * pr_spread + 0.15 * pr_persistence + 0.1 * pr_severity), 1) AS score FROM ranked ORDER BY score DESC, bursts DESC, pattern_id

sql: SELECT s.b AS bucket_start, count(x.t) AS bursts FROM generate_series(date_trunc('week', TIMESTAMP '2005-12-01 00:00:00'), TIMESTAMP '2006-03-01 00:00:00', interval '7 days') s(b) LEFT JOIN (SELECT b.start_ts AS t FROM bursts b JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = b.dataset AND p.pattern_id = b.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = p.dataset AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = p.dataset AND j.pattern_id = p.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 AND p.problem_lines > 0 AND b.dataset = 'apache' AND b.start_ts >= '2005-12-01 00:00:00' AND b.start_ts < '2006-03-01 00:00:00') x ON date_trunc('week', x.t) = s.b GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT round(regr_slope(bursts, i), 3) AS slope, round(avg(bursts) FILTER (WHERE i < 14 / 2.0), 2) AS first_half_mean, round(avg(bursts) FILTER (WHERE i >= 14 / 2.0), 2) AS second_half_mean, sum(bursts) AS total FROM (SELECT row_number() OVER (ORDER BY bucket_start) - 1 AS i, bursts FROM (SELECT s.b AS bucket_start, count(x.t) AS bursts FROM generate_series(date_trunc('week', TIMESTAMP '2005-12-01 00:00:00'), TIMESTAMP '2006-03-01 00:00:00', interval '7 days') s(b) LEFT JOIN (SELECT b.start_ts AS t FROM bursts b JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = b.dataset AND p.pattern_id = b.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = p.dataset AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = p.dataset AND j.pattern_id = p.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 AND p.problem_lines > 0 AND b.dataset = 'apache' AND b.start_ts >= '2005-12-01 00:00:00' AND b.start_ts < '2006-03-01 00:00:00') x ON date_trunc('week', x.t) = s.b GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1))

SELECT team, round(regr_slope(n, i), 3) AS slope, sum(n) AS bursts FROM (SELECT t.team, s.i, count(x.t) AS n FROM (SELECT row_number() OVER (ORDER BY b) - 1 AS i, b FROM generate_series(date_trunc('week', TIMESTAMP '2005-12-01 00:00:00'), TIMESTAMP '2006-03-01 00:00:00', interval '7 days') s(b)) s CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT coalesce(o.team, 'unowned') AS team FROM bursts b JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = b.dataset AND p.pattern_id = b.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = p.dataset AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = p.dataset AND j.pattern_id = p.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 AND p.problem_lines > 0 AND b.dataset = 'apache' AND b.start_ts >= '2005-12-01 00:00:00' AND b.start_ts < '2006-03-01 00:00:00') t LEFT JOIN (SELECT b.start_ts AS t, coalesce(o.team, 'unowned') AS team FROM bursts b JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = b.dataset AND p.pattern_id = b.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = p.dataset AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = p.dataset AND j.pattern_id = p.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND j.p_problem >= 0.5 AND p.problem_lines > 0 AND b.dataset = 'apache' AND b.start_ts >= '2005-12-01 00:00:00' AND b.start_ts < '2006-03-01 00:00:00') x ON date_trunc('week', x.t) = s.b AND x.team = t.team GROUP BY 1, 2) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY bursts DESC

On combo (single node), the morning of 2005-12-06 was dominated by kernel Out of Memory kills, which ran from 00:00:16 until 12:02:46. After 1035.0 seconds with no logged lines, the logs show a graceful reboot sequence starting at 12:20:03. The reboot is not a new problem pattern: OOM kills have recurred for weeks.
Scope: Dataset linux, node combo, 2005-12-06 00:00:00 → 12:30:00 (plus 12:28:50 onward and whole-dataset history for pattern 700495). The first search_logs, facet and context samples are truncated, so counts come from total_matches, facet and pattern_history rather than the sampled rows.
In 2005-12-06 00:00:00 → 12:30:00 there are 837 log lines on 1 node (combo), first at 00:00:16 and last at 12:28:50. 639 of them are from the kernel component.
Pattern 700495 (Out of Memory: Killed process) accounts for 397 of the 837 log lines, first at 00:00:16 and last at 12:02:46. Examples: 'Out of Memory: Killed process 7395 (httpd).' at 00:00:16, then httpd and python victims every few minutes; at 00:27:00-00:27:09 sendmail (7135, 7270) and mrtg (7472) were killed.
At 00:27:23 the kernel logged 'httpd: page allocation failure. order:0, mode:0x1d2' followed by 'Call Trace:' and frames such as __alloc_pages+0x274/0x281. The facet shows 4 lines of pattern 700503 in the window.
Searching from 00:30:00 onward, the first log line is at 01:25:26 ('Out of Memory: Killed process 7479 (httpd).'), and OOM lines continue (e.g. 02:16:58, process 7712 (httpd)).
Before the reboot: the last OOM line is 12:02:46 'Out of Memory: Killed process 9864 (diskcheck).', preceded at 12:02:41 by 9853 (mrtg), at 12:02:40 by 9715 (sendmail) and at 12:02:32 by 9544 (sendmail).
No log lines follow 12:02:46 for 1035.0 seconds: the closest later line is 12:20:01 on combo, gpm: '*** info [mice.c(1766)]: '.
At the reboot: 12:20:03 gdm 'Master rebooting...', 12:20:08 shutdown 'shutting down for system reboot', 12:20:14 init 'Switching to runlevel: 6'.
During shutdown several services logged failures: 12:20:20 messagebus 'messagebus shutdown failed', 12:20:29 'xfs shutdown failed', 12:20:29 'jserver shutdown failed', 12:20:31 'Stopping MySQL:  failed', 12:21:10 'named shutdown failed', 12:20:50 'sm-client shutdown failed', 12:21:21 'rpc.statd shutdown failed' and 'portmap shutdown failed'. Others (atd, privoxy, cups, httpd, squid, sshd, sendmail, smartd, snmpd, xinetd, crond, apmd, ntpd) reported shutdown succeeded or exited.
After the reboot: at 12:22:57 'syslogd 1.4.1: restart.' and the kernel banner 'Linux version 2.6.5-1.358 (bhcompile@bugs.build.redhat.com) ...' appear, along with '126MB LOWMEM available.' and 'Kernel command line: ro root=LABEL=/ rhgb quiet'. The last line in the window is 12:28:50 ntpd 'kernel time sync enabled 0001'.
After 12:28:50 the next logged lines in the sample are named at 17:24:19 ('starting BIND 9.2.3 -u named -t /var/named/chroot'), with no OOM lines in that sample.
This is recurring, not new: pattern 700495 has 133 bursts and 10404 lines on 1 node from 2005-11-15T04:30:29 to 2005-12-09T04:58:54, with 124 bursts before 2005-12-06. The median gap between bursts is 1:14:50.
Against the usual rate: 2005-12-06 had 4 bursts started and 397 lines for pattern 700495, versus 12 bursts and 816 lines on 2005-12-05 and 7 bursts and 960 lines on 2005-12-03. 2005-12-07 had 0 bursts and 0 lines, and 2005-12-08 had 3 bursts and 56 lines.
Hypothesis: The node is chronically short of memory (the boot log shows 126MB LOWMEM available), so the OOM killer repeatedly kills httpd, python, sendmail and mrtg. The reboot at 12:20 may have been an operator response to this, since it follows a graceful shutdown path rather than a crash. Would confirm: Memory/swap metrics for combo before 12:02, the httpd worker limit/config, and a change or operator record for the 12:20 reboot. A drop in OOM lines after the reboot would support it, but the later sample shows OOM bursts on 2005-12-08 and 2005-12-09.
Unknown: The logs do not state why the reboot was issued or who issued it.
Unknown: Root cause of the memory exhaustion (leak, load, undersized RAM) is not in these logs.
Unknown: Why no log lines appear between 12:02:46 and 12:20:01 (1035.0 seconds) is not established.
Unknown: Customer impact or downtime duration is not in the logs.
Unknown: Whether the shutdown failures (MySQL, named, xfs, messagebus, etc.) matter is unknown: they may be services that were already dead after OOM kills.
Next step: Run count_by on component/process name for pattern 700495 on linux, 2005-12-06 00:00 → 12:03, to see which processes were killed most (httpd vs python vs sendmail/mrtg). — The sample shows mostly httpd and python victims; the full distribution is needed for the 397 OOM lines.
Next step: Query linux for 'shutdown failed' lines (pattern 700523, 700525, 700524, 700526, 700528, 700435, 700529, 700530) across 2005-11-15 → 2005-12-09 and compare with other reboots. — Eight services logged shutdown failed at 12:20-12:21; checking history shows whether this is normal for combo or specific to this reboot.
Next step: Inspect httpd configuration (worker/MaxClients) and memory/swap sizing on combo, and check the OOM bursts on 2005-12-08 and 2005-12-09 with search_logs on pattern 700495. — OOM kills continued as a recurring pattern with bursts on 2005-12-08 and 2005-12-09, so the reboot did not clearly clear it.

On combo, the morning was dominated by repeated kernel Out of Memory kills of httpd, python and a few other processes, from 00:00:16 until the last one at 12:02:46. At 12:20:03 gdm logged "Master rebooting..." and a normal shutdown followed, then the box restarted at 12:22:57 and services came back up. The logs show an orderly reboot, but not why it was triggered.
Scope: linux dataset, node combo (the only node), 2005-12-06 00:00:00 → 12:30:00 (some queries to 13:00:00 or 09:00:00 → 12:30:00). 837 log lines in the window. Searches returned 50-row samples (truncated), so counts come from count_by and trend, not the samples.
The window holds 837 log lines from 1 node (combo). The first is at 2005-12-06 00:00:16 and the last at 12:28:50. 639 of the 837 log lines are from the kernel component.
397 log lines match "Out of Memory" in the window, from 2005-12-06 00:00:16 to 12:02:46. Hourly counts run from 15 (08:00 hour) to 52 (02:00 hour), and the 12:00 hour has 16.
The OOM kills come in bursts about every five minutes. Examples: 00:00:16, 00:05:18, 00:10:24, 00:15:25, 00:20:18, 00:25:27 and, later, 11:30:23, 11:35:24, 11:40:17, 11:45:17, 11:50:35, 11:55:14, 12:00:14. The processes are mostly httpd and python, for example "Out of Memory: Killed process 7395 (httpd)." and "Out of Memory: Killed process 7400 (python)."
At 00:27:00 to 00:27:09 the OOM kills hit sendmail (processes 7135 and 7270) and mrtg (process 7472). At 00:27:23 the kernel logged "httpd: page allocation failure. order:0, mode:0x1d2", followed by a "Call Trace:" (__alloc_pages, do_page_cache_readahead, filemap_nopage, do_page_fault).
The last OOM burst before the reboot ends with sendmail (processes 9544 and 9715), mrtg (9853) and diskcheck (9864) being killed at 12:02:32 to 12:02:46. The final line is "Out of Memory: Killed process 9864 (diskcheck)." at 12:02:46.
Between that last OOM line (12:02:46) and the next line at 12:20:01 (gpm) the node logged nothing. From 12:20:01 the lines are: "*** info [mice.c(1766)]: " and "imps2: Auto-detected intellimouse PS/2" (gpm), then at 12:20:03 gdm "Master rebooting...", at 12:20:08 "shutting down for system reboot", and at 12:20:14 init "Switching to runlevel: 6".
During shutdown, 7 services logged "shutdown failed": messagebus (12:20:20), xfs and jserver (12:20:29), sm-client (12:20:50), named (12:21:10), rpc.statd and portmap (12:21:21). Other daemons logged "shutdown succeeded". Kernel logging ended with "Kernel log daemon terminating." at 12:21:22 and "klogd shutdown succeeded" at 12:21:26.
The restart is at 12:22:57: "1.4.1: restart." (syslogd), "syslogd startup succeeded", then "Linux version 2.6.5-1.358 (bhcompile@bugs.build.redhat.com) (gcc version 3.3.3 20040412 (Red Hat Linux 3.3.3-7)) #1 Sat May 8 09:04:50 EDT 2004". That is 1211.0 seconds after the last OOM line.
After boot, the kernel logged "Memory: 125312k/129720k available (1540k kernel code, 3860k reserved, 599k data, 144k init, 0k highmem)" and "Failure registering capabilities with the kernel" at 12:22:58.
After the restart, xinetd logged "bind failed (Address already in use (errno = 98)). service = telnet" and "Service telnet failed to start and is deactivated." at 12:23:19. httpd logged "httpd startup succeeded" at 12:24:08. The last ntpd lines in the window are "kernel time sync disabled 0041" at 12:27:44 and "kernel time sync enabled 0001" at 12:28:50.
The 12:00 hour has 389 log lines, against 15 to 78 log lines in each of the other twelve hourly buckets of the morning.
Hypothesis: Possible cause: memory exhaustion on a small-RAM host (about 129720k) from httpd and python processes that keep respawning every five minutes. This caused the OOM kills, and the reboot may have been an operator response (the graceful shutdown path suggests a manual or scripted reboot, not a crash). Would confirm: Run count_by on the OOM kill body (process name) over several days. Check whether OOM kills resume after 12:28:50 on 2005-12-06 and whether the 5-minute cadence matches a cron job or monitor (mrtg/diskcheck/python). Also check who issued the reboot (admin login or su/gdm lines before 12:20:03).
Unknown: Whether the OOM bursts began before 00:00:16 on 2005-12-06 is not established, so new versus recurring is not known. No earlier days were checked.
Unknown: There is no baseline in these results for the usual OOM rate on combo.
Unknown: The logs do not say who or what triggered the reboot, or why the 7 services failed to shut down.
Unknown: Customer impact, downtime and cost are not in the logs.
Unknown: Only one node (combo) appears, so spread to other hosts cannot be assessed from this dataset.

Next step: Search for admin or session activity (su, gdm, sshd) in the minutes before 12:20:03, and look at why messagebus, xfs, named, rpc.statd and portmap reported "shutdown failed". — The reboot was graceful ("Master rebooting...", "Switching to runlevel: 6") and its initiator is not shown in the logs.
